_meta.status: DESIGN DATA. Not wired in. A developer implements from docs/design/market-npcs.md.
rules: Every in-game string is 80 characters or fewer, plain words, {name} for the player.
Every era label has label History, Tradition or Invented plus a year or Legend.
No real deity appears as a shopkeeper, a name or a joke.
Hunt soldiers are not market NPCs.
_meta.how_to_read: eras[era].variants[archetype] holds names, goods, barks, talk root line and rumour. archetypes[] holds the era-neutral talk replies, task, reactions and mood barks. Tasks and reactions use the archetype id.
_meta.line_fields: barks[], talk, rumour, role_name, goods[].name, labels[].text are era lines. Other lines live in archetypes[], ui, standing, hunt_alert.
_meta.assets_note: Audio barks need captions. Child anklet needs a visual cue as well as a jingle.

talk.label: Talk
talk.does: Opens the 2 to 3 step talk tree.

ask.label: Ask
ask.when: NPC has an unshared rumour or hint, and standing is not Shadowed
ask.does: Gives the rumour line. A second Ask gives a repeat hint only if the NPC is Warm.

trade.label: Trade
trade.when: variant.goods is not empty and NPC is not hostile
trade.does: Buy and sell at standing-adjusted prices. Sell price is 50 percent of base price.

help.label: Help
help.when: NPC task is available, active, or ready to hand in
help.does: Offers, tracks and completes the NPC's tiny side task.

rules: Show only choices that apply. Never show a greyed choice.
If more than 4 apply, drop in this order: Ask repeat, Help when no task, then keep Talk.
Talk is always present, so the menu has between 1 and 4 buttons.
Each button is at least 44 px tall. Number keys 1 to 4 choose. Esc closes.
The menu pauses the world and the level clock (WCAG 2.2.1).

world_actions.label: Greet
world_actions.effect: Namaste (hands joined) or nod. Sets that NPC to Warm for 2 minutes. No standing change.

world_actions.label: Follow
world_actions.effect: The NPC walks beside the player for up to 60 seconds. Used by tasks (elder, child). They refuse if Wary.

world_actions.label: Give
world_actions.input: Choose an item, then tap the NPC
world_actions.effect: Hands over one item. Standing +1 once per NPC per level. Also ends an angry NPC's anger (forgive window).

world_actions.label: Take
world_actions.input: Tap the toss prompt or pick up from the ground
world_actions.effect: Catch an item an NPC tosses (shopkeeper toss, child's ball) or pick up a dropped item. Never costs standing.

world_actions.label: Shove
world_actions.effect: A short push. Blocked on protected NPCs. See reactions.

world_actions.label: Take unseen
world_actions.input: Hold Do on a stall item while the NPC is looking away
world_actions.effect: Takes one item without paying. Blocked on protected NPCs. See witness rules.

world_actions.label: Strike
world_actions.input: Open hand, light cut key (J), unarmed only
world_actions.effect: Open-hand blow. Staggers the NPC. Never damages. Never uses a weapon on a bystander. Blocked on protected NPCs.

verbs.protected_rule: Shove, steal and hit are refused. The button shows the blocked line and nothing happens. No standing change. This is a rule of respect, not a penalty.
verbs.hunt_rule: Hunt soldiers (grey cord) are not market NPCs. Shoving or fighting them never changes Dharma standing.

standing.name: Dharma standing
standing.one_line: Kind acts light your lamp. Harm makes it dim.
standing.reset: start of each level (see open question)
standing.icon_spec: Lamp icon beside a flame. Flame height 0 to 4 plus a text word and, on focus, the number. Never colour alone.

changes.note: Once per NPC per level. Item must be a real item or coin.
Pull up a fallen NPC, return a dropped item, share water.
Give stolen item back to its owner.
The first witnessed shove each level is a free warning: 0.
Dharma sees all, but a smaller mark.
Shoving or catching a marked task-thief is lawful. No change.

standing.recovery: Below 0, standing rises by 1 every 3 minutes toward 0. It never rises above 0 on its own. Positive standing does not decay.
standing.npc_memory: An NPC you harmed stays Wary: no trade, no help, until you Give them something or finish a Help for another NPC nearby. Wary does not change global standing.
standing.guard_catch: When a hostile guard catches the player: stolen items go back, the player pays up to 5 coins, no jail, no death, standing unchanged. Guards give up after 10 seconds out of sight.
standing.accessibility: Standing change shows a caption like 'Your lamp dims a little' and a short sound with a visual pulse. Reduced motion: no pulse, text only.

sees_when: NPC is awake and not in a menu
player is inside the NPC's 120 degree view cone
no wall or stall blocks the line
witness.victim: The victim always counts as a witness for shove and hit. For steal, the victim counts only if not facing away or after noticing (see below).

hearing.effect: Hearers turn and look. They become witnesses only if they then see the player within 3 seconds.

witness.crowd_cover: With 3 or more NPCs within 2 m and the crouch skill, sight_m drops to 4. Not available before the crouch skill.
witness.unwitnessed_steal: No one saw: standing -1 now. The victim notices after 20 seconds and shouts once, without a chase.
witness.children: Child witnesses count the same as adults. They never chase.
witness.guards: A guard who hears a shout walks to the spot. He turns hostile only if he sees the act or the player holds the stolen item in view within 10 seconds.
witness.cools_off: A chase ends when the player is out of sight for 10 seconds or 20 m away.
witness.hunt: Hunt soldiers ignore market crimes and do not report. Civilians still react to fights nearby by fleeing.

hunt_alert.trigger: Any Hunt soldier within 15 m draws a weapon.
hunt_alert.npc_response: Civilians stop idle barks, flee to shelter points, and say one cover line. Menus show 'Not now' until the area is clear for 8 seconds.
lines: Run! Away from the grey cords!

items.name: Road lamp
items.effect: light source; guides the hint arrow at night

items.name: Clay pot
items.effect: carry water or throw to draw eyes (no damage)

items.name: Rope
items.effect: use at marked posts and ledges

ui.ask_warning: Be careful, {name}. Folk are wary of you.
ui.task_ready: I have it. Here you go.
ui.wary: I do not trust you now.
ui.guard_caught: Hand it back. Pay the fine.
ui.guard_apology: Sorry, officer. It will not happen again.
ui.guard_accept: Good. Do not do it again.
ui.guard_receive_note: A note for me? Thank you.
ui.shelter: Stay inside! It is not safe!

archetypes.label: Lamp seller
archetypes.personality: Patient and chatty. Fusses over fire safety. Hates waste.

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.reply: I sell light. Small trade, good work.

next.label: Is it hard work?
next.reply: Wicks and oil all day. I like it.

choices.label: How is trade?
choices.reply: Slow when folk are afraid. Steady otherwise.

task.offer: Carry this lit lamp to my sister's stall? Keep it burning.
task.hint: Shield the flame. Do not run too fast.
task.done: Still lit! Thank you, {name}. Take this.
task.fail: It went out. No harm. Try once more.

gift.line: A gift? That is kind. Thank you.

mood_barks.cold: Move along. I have no light for you.

archetypes.label: Spice or pepper seller
archetypes.personality: Sharp with numbers, warm once trust is earned. Proud of fair weights.

choices.label: Is it good quality?
choices.reply: Taste it. My name is on every bag.

next.label: Where is it from?
next.reply: Far off. It came by road and by boat.

choices.label: Any advice?
choices.reply: Spice a little, never a lot.

task.offer: A thief took my pouch! Catch him, {name}!
task.hint: He ran the lane. Cut him off at the corner.
task.done: My pouch! Take some spice for your trouble.
task.fail: He got away. Thank you for trying.

gift.line: For me? You are generous. Thank you.

mood_barks.cold: I will weigh this carefully. Very carefully.

archetypes.label: Potter
archetypes.personality: Calm and exact. Hates rushing. Talks to the clay.

choices.label: How is a pot made?
choices.reply: Clay, water, a steady hand, then fire.

next.label: Is it hard?
next.reply: Years of breaking pots. Then fewer.

choices.label: Which pot is best?
choices.reply: The one that does its job. Plain is fine.

task.offer: Carry these two pots to the well without a crack.
task.hint: Walk, do not run. Pots break if you fall.
task.done: Both whole! Keep one for your trouble.
task.fail: One cracked. It happens. Come again.

gift.line: How kind. A pot for you someday.

mood_barks.warm: Welcome, {name}. This one is for you.
mood_barks.cold: I count every pot. Do not touch.

archetypes.label: Cloth merchant
archetypes.personality: Smooth talker, honest underneath. Notices everyone's clothes.

choices.label: What do you sell?
choices.reply: Cloth, cord and bandage. All strong.

next.label: Is the rope good?
next.reply: It held a cart once. Ask the cart.

choices.label: Any news?
choices.reply: Everyone buys cloth. Everyone talks.

task.offer: Take this cloth bundle to the scribe's table.
task.hint: He sits near the busiest stall.
task.done: Delivered? Good. Here is a coil of rope.
task.fail: Not delivered? No matter. Try again.

gift.line: A gift? You flatter me. Thank you.

mood_barks.warm: Welcome, {name}! A good price for you.
mood_barks.cold: Prices are firm today. Very firm.

archetypes.label: Fruit seller
archetypes.personality: Cheerful. Gives small tastes. Hates waste and bruises.

choices.label: Is the fruit fresh?
choices.reply: Picked this morning. Taste one.

next.label: How do you pick well?
next.reply: Press gently. Smell. Trust your nose.

choices.label: Any news?
choices.reply: Fruit sellers hear everything.

task.offer: My fruit rolled away! Please bring back three.
task.hint: They roll downhill. Look near the lane edge.
task.done: Three! Ripe and whole. Eat one, {name}.
task.fail: Not all found. Thanks for looking.

gift.line: Oh, thank you! Take a fruit back.

mood_barks.warm: Dear {name}! The ripest one is yours.

archetypes.label: Water carrier
archetypes.personality: Quiet and steady. Knows every lane and every well.

choices.label: Where is the well?
choices.reply: Past the lanes. I will point the way.

next.label: Is it a long walk?
next.reply: Every day. My feet know it by heart.

choices.label: Any news?
choices.reply: I walk the whole market. I hear things.

task.offer: Carry this water pot to the guard post. Slowly now.
task.done: Cool and full. You have good hands.
task.fail: It spilled. Fill it and try again.

mood_barks.cold: Water is for those who ask kindly.

archetypes.label: Child
archetypes.personality: Curious, quick, a little bold. Asks big questions.

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.reply: I am me! Who are you?

choices.label: Can you tell me something?
choices.reply: Maybe. If you share a sweet.

task.offer: My sister's anklet fell. Can you find it?
task.hint: It jingles! Listen near the stalls.
task.done: Found it! Thank you, {name}! Take this.
task.fail: Not found yet. Please look again!

mood_barks.warm: {name}! You came back! Play with me!
mood_barks.cold: Mama says not to talk to you.

archetypes.label: Elder
archetypes.personality: Gentle, wise, a little stubborn. Loves to talk, slowly.

choices.label: How are you?
choices.reply: Old, but still walking.

next.label: What have you learned?
next.reply: Kindness costs little and pays back well.

choices.label: Any advice?
choices.reply: Walk slow. Look around. Help someone.

task.offer: Walk me to the bench by the shrine? Slowly.
task.done: Thank you. A kind arm beats a stick.
task.fail: We did not get there. Another time.

mood_barks.cold: Hm. I hear you have been unkind.

archetypes.label: Musician
archetypes.personality: Dreamy, generous, easily startled. Pays attention to moods.

choices.label: What do you play?
choices.reply: Whatever the street asks for.

next.label: Teach me?
next.reply: Listen first. The hands come later.

choices.label: Any news?
choices.reply: Songs travel faster than news.

task.offer: My string broke. Bring a cord from the cloth stall?
task.hint: Ask the cloth seller. Say it is for music.
task.done: Sweet! Here is a thank you, {name}.
task.fail: No cord yet. I will wait.

gift.line: Thank you! I will play for you.

mood_barks.warm: {name}! I wrote a song for you.
mood_barks.cold: I will not play for you.

archetypes.label: Scribe

look.garment: plain long wrap, ink-stained or knotted cords

archetypes.personality: Precise, dry humour. Writes things down so no one lies.

choices.label: What do you write?
choices.reply: Names, counts and messages.

next.label: Can you read this?
next.reply: Show me. I will tell you what it says.

choices.label: Any news?
choices.reply: I write what I hear. Mostly.

task.offer: Take this note to the guard post, {name}.
task.hint: Keep it dry. Hand it to the guard.
task.done: Received. Take this for the walk.
task.fail: The note did not arrive. Try again.

mood_barks.cold: I have nothing to write for you.

archetypes.label: Blacksmith
archetypes.personality: Gruff, fair, proud of work. Respects anyone who works hard.

choices.label: What do you make?
choices.reply: Hooks, nails and tool tips. Honest iron.

next.label: Is it hot work?
next.reply: Hot, loud and good. I would not swap.

choices.label: Any advice?
choices.reply: Learn one thing well. Then another.

task.offer: Work my bellows for a moment? Hold Do.

shove.line: Hey! Do that again, and I push back!

hit.line: Enough! I push harder than you!

mood_barks.warm: {name}! Come, share a cup with me.
mood_barks.cold: I do not work for thieves.

archetypes.label: Temple priest or pandit

look.garment: plain wrap, sacred thread or beads as the era fits

archetypes.personality: Calm, kind, unhurried. Never pushes. Never sells anything.

choices.label: What do you do here?
choices.reply: I tend the flame and keep the peace.

next.label: May I rest here?
next.reply: Yes. All are welcome. Sit and be quiet.

choices.label: Any blessing?
choices.reply: Take it freely. It costs nothing.

task.offer: Please set three small lamps on the shrine steps.
task.hint: Left, middle, right. Take your time.
task.done: Peace to you. May your road stay open.
task.fail: The lamps are not set. Come again.

gift.line: Thank you. May it return to you.

mood_barks.warm: Peace to you, {name}. Your lamp is bright.
mood_barks.cold: Peace to you, even so. Be gentler.

archetypes.label: Travelling storyteller
archetypes.personality: Warm, dramatic, curious. Collects sayings and gives credit.

choices.label: Tell me a tale.
choices.reply: Once, a road stayed open all night.

next.label: Why that tale?
next.reply: Because roads keep the best secrets.

choices.label: Any news?
choices.reply: News and tales walk together.

task.offer: Ask three people for a saying. I will weave them in.
task.hint: Anyone will do. Elders know many.
task.done: Lovely! A fine tale grows. Here, for you.
task.fail: Not enough sayings yet. Keep asking.

shove.line: Oh! Not in the middle of a tale!

mood_barks.warm: {name}! I added you to my tale.
mood_barks.cold: I will tell a different tale about you.

archetypes.label: Town guard
archetypes.personality: Stern but fair. Dislikes crowds. Likes honest people.

choices.label: What do you guard?
choices.reply: The lanes, the gate, and the peace.

next.label: Any trouble?
next.reply: Not yet. Let us keep it that way.

choices.label: Any advice?
choices.reply: Stay in the lit lanes. Be kind.

task.offer: Found a purse. Return it to the fruit seller?
task.done: Honest of you. Take this staff on loan.
task.fail: Purse not returned. Try once more.

gift.line: Gifts to a guard? Careful. But thanks.

hit.line: That is it. Stop right there!

mood_barks.warm: Good to see you, {name}. Walk safe.
mood_barks.cold: I am watching you. Keep your hands still.

hastinapur.name: Hastinapur, Dvapara Yuga
hastinapur.setting: Night, lamp rows, canal lane, bridge bell. Tense but human.
hastinapur.dress: Plain wraps and shoulder cloths, undyed to light dyes, no stitched tunics.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Painted Grey Ware at Hastinapur Period II (B. B. Lal): the potter's grey bowls.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Iron appears at Painted Grey Ware sites of the Ganga plain. Not checked here.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Farming and cattle at Painted Grey Ware sites. Exact crops not checked.

labels.label: History
labels.text: No coins or known script in these layers. Our tally knots are a story device.

labels.label: Tradition
labels.text: Priests tending a household fire in the Vedic tradition. Shown with respect.

labels.label: Tradition
labels.text: Road reciters of tales, as in the epic tradition. No epic figure is named.

labels.label: Invented
labels.text: The Lamp Bazaar crowd, the market folk, their names, tasks and clay tokens.

labels.label: Tradition
labels.text: The eve of the great war (story frame, from docs/story.md).

labels.label: Invented
labels.text: Clay lamps for sale. Lamp use in this period not checked.

labels.label: Invented
labels.text: Woven cloth and cord for sale. Fabrics of the period not checked.

barks: Lamps! Light your way before the oil runs short.
Clay lamps, warm in the hand. Come close.
Night is long, {name}. A flame is short.
Mind the oil. It spills and it burns.
Fewer buyers tonight. Everyone hurries home.
A lamp lit here guides a stranger home.
lamp_seller.talk: Lamps for the night, {name}? Take your time. Or none at all.
lamp_seller.rumour: Men with grey cords on their wrists. Not the city watch. Keep clear.

barks: Salt and mustard seed! Fresh from the field.
A pinch of ginger warms a cold night.
Grain is dear this season. Salt is not.
Smell this, {name}. It lifts a tired heart.
Seeds by the handful. Fair measure, always.
My scale is true. Ask anyone in the row.
spice_seller.talk: Salt, mustard, ginger. What does your cook need, {name}?
spice_seller.rumour: The canal bridge lifts at the bell. Cross before it rings.

barks: Grey bowls, smooth as river stone!
Hand-turned, fired hard. They will not leak.
Careful near my shelf, {name}. Clay breaks.
A pot holds water, grain, or a long night.
The kiln is still warm. Come see.
Every pot has a thumb mark. That one is mine.
potter.talk: Grey bowls and water pots. Pick one up, {name}. Go gently.
potter.rumour: Stall roofs are sound. When the lane fills, go over it.

barks: Woven cloth! Soft wool, plain weave.
Cords and cloth strips. Strong and cheap.
A cloth wrap keeps off the night chill.
Rope for a roof, a cart, or a rescue.
Feel the weave, {name}. No flaws.
Dye dries slow in this damp air.
cloth_merchant.talk: Cloth and cord, {name}. Tell me what you need to carry.
cloth_merchant.rumour: The bridge bell hangs from a rope. Cut it, and you gain a little time.

barks: Sweet fruit! Ripe tonight, gone tomorrow.
Jamun, ber, mango. Taste one, {name}.
Fruit mends a tired runner. It is true.
Cool fruit for a hot-footed night.
Mind the rolling ones! They run off.
Last of the day's basket. A fair price.
fruit_seller.talk: Ripe fruit, {name}. A bite will keep you running.
fruit_seller.rumour: A child carries a lantern through the rows. Mind the little flame.

barks: Water! Cool water from the deep well.
A sip for the road, {name}?
My pots are heavy. My feet know every step.
The canal is loud tonight. The well is quiet.
Water holds no grudge. Drink.
Lamp work is thirsty work. Drink up.
water_carrier.talk: Water is one token, {name}. Or a kind word.
water_carrier.rumour: The canal lane is long and crowded. Do not stop to fight there.

barks: Look! My lantern is lit!
Race you to the well, {name}!
Why is everyone so quiet tonight?
I can hop on one foot. Watch me!
The big lamps are pretty from up here.
Mother says stay close. I am close!
child.talk: Hello, {name}! Do you want to see my lantern?
child.rumour: I saw men with grey string on their wrists. They looked cross.

barks: I have seen many nights like this one.
Sit awhile, {name}. The road waits.
Young feet. How I miss them.
Be kind to strangers. Roads remember.
The old well has never run dry. Not once.
Hurry slowly, child. It saves time.
elder.talk: Namaste, {name}. Walk slowly. The city is restless tonight.
elder.rumour: When the bell rings, the bridge lifts. Cross while it is low.

barks: A tune for the tired. Pay what you like.
Flute and drum. The night wants music.
Even a worried city likes a song.
Listen, {name}. That one is for the road.
My drum keeps time. Your feet can too.
Soft tonight. The lanes are listening.
musician.talk: A song, {name}? Or news? I carry both.
musician.rumour: The east gate opens on a captain's word. Find an honest one.

barks: Counts kept, knots tied, grain tallied.
Ten sacks in, nine out. Someone is hungry.
I tie a knot for every promise made.
Messages carried. Tallies kept. Ask me.
Mind the knots, {name}. They are my memory.
A fair count makes a fair market.
scribe.talk: I keep the tallies. Need a count or a message, {name}?
scribe.rumour: Village grain runs low. A plea at the east gate could feed them.

barks: Hammer and fire! Hooks, blades, nails.
Iron is hard. So is the work.
Stand back, {name}. Sparks bite.
The bellows are tired. So am I.
A good hook holds a roof, a cart, a life.
Strike while it glows. Never after.
blacksmith.talk: Mind the sparks, {name}. What do you need mended?
blacksmith.rumour: Those spear points were not made here. Wrong shape, wrong hands.

barks: May your road be safe, traveller.
The flame is tended. Be at peace.
Come, share the evening quiet.
A kind word is also an offering.
Walk with care. Night hides many things.
Peace to this city, and to you.
priest.talk: Namaste, {name}. May the warmth of the flame go with you.
priest.rumour: Keep to the lit lanes. Dark corners hide trouble tonight.

barks: Gather round! A tale of the long road!
Once, a lamp walked all night. Listen!
Hush, children. The best part is next.
Tales cost nothing. Listening takes a little time.
A road remembers who walked it, {name}.
Shall I tell of the river and the lamp?
storyteller.talk: A story, {name}? I know the river tale and the lamp tale.
storyteller.rumour: In my tale, the swift cross the bridge before the bell.

barks: Keep moving. Keep the lanes clear.
Quiet night. Let us keep it so.
The watch changes at the bell.
Mind the crowd, {name}. No pushing.
Lost? Ask. Tempted to steal? Think twice.
Grey cords? Not ours. Stay clear of them.
town_guard.talk: Evening, {name}. The watch is on. How can I help?
town_guard.rumour: The bridge bell shuts the canal. After it rings, no one crosses.

pataliputra.name: Pataliputra, Mauryan empire
pataliputra.place: Ganga wharf lanes in monsoon rain
pataliputra.setting: Rain, wharf planks, timber yard, palisade lane, sluice house.
pataliputra.dress: Wraps, shoulder cloths, oiled rain cloths, straw hats.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Punch-marked silver coins (karshapana) in the Mauryan period. Pages not read.

labels.label: History
labels.year: c. late 4th-early 3rd century BCE (as reported, unverified)
labels.text: Megasthenes, via later writers, describes officials who oversee the city.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Brahmi script on Ashokan edicts. Everyday letter writing is our assumption.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Northern Black Polished Ware, a fine glossy pottery.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Ashokan edict records wells dug along roads (docs/story.md).

labels.label: History
labels.text: Ashoka patronised Buddhist monks; other teachers and traditions lived alongside.

labels.label: Tradition
labels.text: Arthashastra covers city watch and night rules. Date and author contested.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Timber wall and palisade at Pataliputra (Megasthenes; Waddell).

labels.label: Invented
labels.text: The rain-market stalls, names and tasks near the Ganga wharf.

barks: Rain lamps! Hooded lamps that keep their flame.
Wet night, dark lane. Buy a light, {name}.
My wicks are dry. Everything else is not.
A lamp saves a stumble. Maybe a fall.
The river is loud tonight. Light helps.
Hooded lamps, plenty of oil. Come in from the rain.
lamp_seller.talk: Rain lamps, {name}. The hood keeps the wind out.
lamp_seller.rumour: Watch lanterns sweep the palisade lane in pairs tonight.

barks: Pepper from the far south! Hot and clean.
Ginger for the damp chest. Rain brings coughs.
Cumin, ginger, pepper. Honest weight.
Weighed true on the marked scale.
Rain ruins loose seed. Mine is wrapped.
Taste a pinch, {name}. No charge.
spice_seller.talk: Pepper came a long way to this stall, {name}. Take some.
spice_seller.rumour: Watchmen see what moves. Stand still in shadow and they pass.

barks: Polished bowls, black as the night river!
Water jars, grain jars. Sound and plain.
Rain ruins the drying rack. Not the fired ware.
Do not lean on the shelf, {name}.
Fired hard, rung true. Hear that? No crack.
A pot outlasts its maker. Choose well.
potter.talk: Fine bowls and plain jars. Tap one, {name}. Hear it ring.
potter.rumour: Timber stacks in the yard stand tall. Good cover, bad footing.

barks: Cotton and wool! Dry cloth for a wet night.
Rain wraps! Oiled cloth and straw hats.
Strong cord for boats and bundles.
Cloth from the east. Weave from the west.
Wrap up, {name}. The river air bites.
Fair price, fair cloth, fair word.
cloth_merchant.talk: Cloth and cord, {name}. Rain is hard on the unready.
cloth_merchant.rumour: Rain-soaked posts swell and slip. Do not linger in the palisade lane.

barks: Jamun and plantain! Sweet in the rain.
Ripe fruit! Wet hands, sweet mouths.
A bite of sweet for a bitter night.
Take two, {name}. They keep the cold off.
From the orchard to your hand by dusk.
Dry basket, wet street. Come under the awning.
fruit_seller.talk: Fruit to warm a wet night, {name}. A bite or two?
fruit_seller.rumour: The sluice house keeps the river gauge. When it climbs, so does worry.

barks: Well water! Clean and cold. No river mud.
The river is brown tonight. My well is clear.
A cup for the road, {name}?
Wells were dug for travellers. Drink.
Rain on my pole, rain on my head.
A full pot is a quiet pot.
water_carrier.talk: Well water, {name}. The river is too muddy to drink tonight.
water_carrier.rumour: Boats are tied double at the wharf. The river is rising, they say.

barks: The rain is so loud! I love it!
Splash! Catch me if you can, {name}!
Boats! So many boats on the river.
I saw a man run with a pouch.
I am not scared of the watch. A little scared.
Do puddles have bottoms? Let me check.
child.talk: Hello! Do you like rain? I like rain.
child.rumour: The timber yard has stacks taller than a house. Good for hiding!

barks: This city was a village once, they say.
Rain again. The river rises, old bones ache.
Be careful in the dark, child.
A kind deed is never wasted.
Sit, {name}. Rest your feet a little.
My knees warn me before the rain does.
elder.talk: Come under the awning, {name}. The night is wet.
elder.rumour: The wall is old wood. Wet wood groans. Listen for it.

barks: Harp and drum! A tune against the rain.
Rain makes the best drum. Listen.
A song keeps spirits up, and mine too.
Pay in coin or in kindness, {name}.
The watch drum beats. Mine beats softer.
Soft song for a hard night.
musician.talk: A tune, {name}? The rain asks for one.
musician.rumour: The watch drum sounds at each turn. Count the beats, then go.

barks: Letters written clear. Names, counts, notes.
Dictate, I will write. Fair price.
Writing dries slow in rain. Patience.
A note carried is a promise kept.
Count twice, write once, {name}.
The wharf is busy. So is my stylus.
scribe.talk: I write letters and keep counts, {name}. What shall I write?
scribe.rumour: The sluice house keeps the water record. Overseer Kshema reads it nightly.

barks: Iron hooks and nails! Hammer all night.
Rain hisses on hot iron. I like the sound.
Stand clear, {name}. Sparks jump.
Boats need nails. Boats need me.
Good iron lasts. Bad iron rusts.
Bellows, coal, patience.
blacksmith.talk: Iron work, {name}. Hooks, nails, tools. What do you need?
blacksmith.rumour: Palisade ties are rusting. Iron rings give way before the wood.

barks: May you be well and free from fear.
Rain falls on all alike. Peace to you.
I walk, and I ask for little.
A gentle word is a gift to everyone.
Be calm, traveller. Calm sees clearly.
May your road be safe, {name}.
priest.talk: Peace be with you, {name}. How can I help on this wet night?
priest.rumour: Walk with calm. The night watch is on edge, and so is the river.

barks: A tale of the river city! Come close!
Once, a quiet foot crossed a loud night.
Rain makes the best tale weather.
Hush, {name}. The tale is about to turn.
A story told is a story saved.
Tales are free. The shelter costs extra.
storyteller.talk: A story, {name}? Of the river, or of the quiet foot?
storyteller.rumour: In my tale, the quiet foot crosses where the loud foot is caught.

barks: Move along. Keep to the lit lanes.
Watch is doubled tonight. Stay clear.
Curfew soon. Home, friends, home.
No pushing at the wharf, {name}.
Questions? Ask. Trouble? Not on my watch.
River wall holds. So do I.
town_guard.talk: Evening, {name}. The night watch is on duty. Need help?
town_guard.rumour: Watch is doubled tonight. Keep out of the palisade lane, traveller.

sangam.name: Sangam pepper road
sangam.place: Hill village stalls on the pepper road, dusk
sangam.setting: Stream bank, rope bridge, goat path, harbour scales at evening tide.
sangam.dress: Light cotton wraps, palm-leaf hats, bead and shell jewellery.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Sangam age poems and trade in Tamilakam (docs/story.md).

labels.label: History
labels.text: Pepper traded to Yavana (Greek and Roman) merchants from a coast harbour.

labels.label: History
labels.year: c. 1st century BCE-3rd century CE (as reported, unverified)
labels.text: Roman coins found in southern India. Used here as a hint of trade only.

labels.label: History
labels.year: c. 3rd century BCE onward (as reported, unverified)
labels.text: Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions, such as Mangulam. Palm leaf writing is Tradition.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Bards with a lute-harp (yazh) in Sangam poems.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Salt traded for grain in Sangam poems. Not used in lines yet.

labels.label: Tradition
labels.text: Bamboo staff practice named for silambu bamboo (silambam).

labels.label: Invented
labels.text: The pepper-road market folk, names, tasks and the caravan.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Black-and-red ware pottery in the south.

barks: Lamps for the hill path! Dusk comes quick.
Bronze or clay. Both burn bright.
Evening tide is near. Light before you go.
A hill road in the dark is a hard road.
Wicks of cotton, oil by the cup.
Take a flame up the pass, {name}.
lamp_seller.talk: Lamps for the pass, {name}? The path gets dark fast.
lamp_seller.rumour: The old rope bridge sways even in calm air. Test each plank.

barks: Black pepper! The best from the hills.
Gold in a sack. Ask the harbour.
Pepper climbs on trees. Yes, trees.
Hill pay, hill pepper. Handle with care.
Smell that, {name}? That is a winter's wages.
Weigh it twice. I always do.
spice_seller.talk: Hill pepper, {name}. A whole season in one sack.
spice_seller.rumour: Sacks must reach the harbour scales before the tide turns.

barks: Jars for grain, jars for water!
Red clay, hill clay. Fired in my own kiln.
Black-and-red ware, plain and strong.
Mind the jars, {name}. Clay is shy.
A cracked jar is a lesson. Mind your elbows.
Fill one at the stream. It stays cool.
potter.talk: Black-and-red jars, {name}. Sturdy for the road.
potter.rumour: The stream bank is slick. Jars and travellers both slip there.

barks: Fine cotton! Light for the hot coast.
Cloth, cord and sack. Everything to carry.
Strong sacks hold pepper. Weak ones spill.
Dyed in plant colours. They hold fast.
A good rope has saved a sack and a life.
Feel the thread, {name}. Even and strong.
cloth_merchant.talk: Cloth, sacks and cord, {name}. What are you carrying?
cloth_merchant.rumour: Ropes do not snap alone. Keep your sacks tied and your eyes up.

barks: Bananas! Sweet jackfruit! Fresh from the grove.
Hill fruit, coast fruit. Taste one, {name}.
A ripe fruit for a hard climb.
Peel it yourself. I only pick.
Fruit is the best pay for a tired back.
Fresh since dawn. Gone by dusk.
fruit_seller.talk: Fruit for the climb, {name}? Take your pick.
fruit_seller.rumour: Goats use the narrow path above the stream. So do worse company.

barks: Spring water! Sweet and cold from the hill.
Drink before the climb, {name}.
The stream runs high. Take water from my jars.
Cool water costs less than a cramp.
Pots on a pole, steps on the stone.
Careful on wet rocks. I know them well.
water_carrier.talk: Spring water, {name}. Drink slowly. The path is steep.
water_carrier.rumour: Rocks near the ledge crumble. Test each step before you trust it.

barks: I can climb the big rock!
Hear the stream? It is singing.
Catch me, {name}! You cannot!
Look, a goat! He is eating my string.
Father says pepper pays for winter.
I counted ten boats at the harbour once.
child.talk: Hello! Do you have a goat? I like goats.
child.rumour: A man on the high rock watched the bridge all morning. He had a bow.

barks: I walked this pass before you were born.
Pepper pays, but patience pays better.
Sit, sit. The harbour can wait a breath.
The hills feed us. Be kind to them.
Mind the old ones on the path, {name}.
My knees say rain. They are never wrong.
elder.talk: Vanakkam, {name}. Walk slowly. The hills teach patience.
elder.rumour: At dusk the tide turns. Sacks must reach the scales before it.

barks: Strings and song! A tune for the road.
The yazh sings of hills and harbours.
A bard eats what the song earns.
Listen, {name}. That one is for the stream.
Sing it once, and the road remembers.
Soft strings tonight. The wind is up.
musician.talk: A song for the pass, {name}? Or news from the harbour?
musician.rumour: I sang for the caravan at dawn. Their master worried about the bridge.

barks: Letters cut on stone, marks on leaf.
A sack counted is a sack kept.
Palm leaf keeps a promise longer than breath.
The harbour scale gives numbers. I write them.
Need a mark? A name? A count?
Mind the stylus, {name}. It scratches deep.
scribe.talk: I keep counts and write names, {name}. What is yours to write?
scribe.rumour: The harbour clerk seals each sack. A sealed sack cannot be argued with.

barks: Iron and fire! Hooks, nails, spear tips.
Charcoal is dear. Iron is dearer.
Stand back, {name}. Sparks fly.
A hook holds a sack. A good one holds a bridge.
Bellows, hammer, patience. That is a smith.
I mend, I do not break. Remember that.
blacksmith.talk: Iron work, {name}. What needs mending or making?
blacksmith.rumour: That rope bridge was strong. Ropes do not snap on their own.

barks: May the hills keep you, traveller.
Flowers at the shrine, peace in the heart.
Come in quietly. Leave worries at the door.
A traveller's blessing costs nothing.
Safe road, kind hands, full heart.
The hill is old. Be gentle with it.
priest.talk: Vanakkam, {name}. May your road be safe and your load light.
priest.rumour: Walk the goat path by day. After dusk the stones are treacherous.

barks: A tale from the hill! A tale from the sea!
Hush now. The best part is the bridge.
My story has a pepper vine and a clever goat.
Sit close, {name}. The wind carries the words.
Tales are cheap. Listening is a gift.
Once, a road stayed open all night...
storyteller.talk: A tale for the road, {name}? Hills, sea, or goats?
storyteller.rumour: In my tale, the staff turns spears. Ask Poonkodi at the bamboo grove.

barks: Keep to the road. Keep sacks in sight.
Harbour watch. We keep the scales honest.
No pushing at the weigh stand, {name}.
Thieves like crowded harbours. Watch your purse.
Slow day. I like slow days.
Report trouble to me. Do not make it.
town_guard.talk: Evening, {name}. The harbour watch is at your service.
town_guard.rumour: Someone is watching the pass. Stay close to the caravan.

gupta.name: Gupta forge road
gupta.place: Roadside stalls beside the forge, near dawn
gupta.setting: Forge yard, gate, shed, bellows, bridge nails due by dawn.
gupta.dress: Stitched cotton and some silk, belts, simple jewellery.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Gupta empire (docs/story.md).

labels.label: History
labels.text: Delhi iron pillar, known for resisting rust.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Gold coins of the Gupta kings, including archer types.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Gold coins show a lute-type instrument (lyrist type). No ruler is shown in game.

labels.label: History
labels.text: A silk-weavers' guild is named in the Mandasor inscription. Pages not read.

labels.label: History
labels.text: Early brick and stone temples, for example at Deogarh and Bhitargaon.

labels.label: Tradition
labels.text: The Dhanurveda, the science of the bow (docs/story.md).

labels.label: Invented
labels.text: The forge-road market folk, names and tasks, and the smith Ayasa's neighbours.

barks: Lamps and wicks! Light the forge road.
Brass lamps, clay lamps. All burn well.
Dawn is far, {name}. A lamp is near.
The forge road is long and dark. Buy light.
Oil is cheap. Falling in a ditch is not.
Smiths use my lamps for night work.
lamp_seller.talk: Lamps for the forge road, {name}? The nights are black.
lamp_seller.rumour: Watch the forge gate at night. Strange men gather near it.

barks: Pepper, ginger, cumin, cardamom!
Spice from the south, salt from the coast.
Warm food for a cold dawn.
A pinch for the soup, a pinch for the road.
Honest weights. Ask anyone on the road.
Pepper keeps well. So do friends, {name}.
spice_seller.talk: Spice for the road, {name}? Or something to warm the pot?
spice_seller.rumour: Raiders were seen near the bridge works. Walk with a crowd.

barks: Pots and pans! Strong, fired, ready!
Water jars, oil jars, cooking pots.
Careful, {name}. A broken pot is a lost coin.
Plain red clay. Plain honest work.
Smiths buy my cooling jars by the dozen.
Clay remembers every thumb.
potter.talk: Pots for the pot, {name}. Take one in your hands.
potter.rumour: The smith wants cooling jars by dawn. Something big is being made.

barks: Cotton and silk! Fine weave, fair price.
Silk for some, cotton for most. Both warm.
Ropes and sacking for the road.
Cord for bundles, cloth for bandages.
Strong cloth, strong stitch, strong word.
Feel the weave, {name}. No flaws.
cloth_merchant.talk: Cloth, cord and bandage, {name}. What do you need?
cloth_merchant.rumour: A rider with a grey cord on his wrist asked about couriers.

barks: Mangoes and pomegranates! Sweet and fresh.
A fruit makes a tired traveller smile.
Pomegranate! Red and juicy.
Eat one now, {name}. Carry one for later.
Fresh from the grove at dawn.
Sweet fruit, small price, big smile.
fruit_seller.talk: Fruit for the road, {name}? A bite heals more than you think.
fruit_seller.rumour: Bridge nails are due by dawn. The village cannot cross without them.

barks: Cool water! Wells along the road.
A sip for the smith, a sip for you.
The road is dusty, {name}. Drink.
Charcoal makes thirst. Water cures it.
Pot on my shoulder, road under my feet.
A drink given today is repaid tomorrow.
water_carrier.talk: Water, {name}. The forge makes everyone thirsty.
water_carrier.rumour: The forge gate is the only way in. Guard it well after dark.

barks: I want to be a smith! Or a drummer!
The anvil is so loud! Bang bang bang!
Race me, {name}! To the big tree!
I saw sparks fly like stars.
My ball went under the cart. Again.
Father says I ask too many questions.
child.talk: Hello! Have you seen the forge? It has fire inside.
child.rumour: Big men with grey string came to the gate. They bought nothing.

barks: I remember when this road was a path.
The forge fire has burned all my life.
Sit with me, {name}. The sun is kind.
Young people hurry. Old people arrive.
A good smith is a good neighbour.
Mind the cart ruts. They are deep.
elder.talk: Namaste, {name}. The road is long. Rest your feet.
elder.rumour: Bridge nails matter more than any sword. People must cross.

barks: Veena and flute! Songs for the road.
Old coins show a lute like mine. I am proud.
A song for the smith. A song for the sparks.
Strings tuned, voice warm, {name}.
The anvil keeps my beat.
Pay in coin, or sing along.
musician.talk: A song, {name}? The anvil keeps time for me.
musician.rumour: The anvils stopped at dusk. When anvils stop, trouble starts.

barks: Letters, deeds, accounts. Written fair.
Palm leaf or bark. Which will you have?
A letter sent is a mind opened.
I write what you say, {name}. No more.
Names and numbers, neatly kept.
The forge orders are mine to keep.
scribe.talk: Letters and accounts, {name}. What shall I write for you?
scribe.rumour: The smith Ayasa promised bridge nails by dawn. The village counts on it.

barks: Iron! Hooks, nails, tools! Fire-fresh!
Iron that does not rust? I would love to know how.
Hammer and tongs! Mind the sparks, {name}.
Good iron makes a good road.
Nails for the bridge are my best work.
Charcoal, bellows, patience.
blacksmith.talk: Mind the sparks, {name}. What can I forge or mend?
blacksmith.rumour: The bellows must work until dawn. The fire cannot sleep.

barks: May you be at peace, traveller.
The small stone shrine is open to all.
Bring a flower, or just bring yourself.
A calm mind walks farther, {name}.
I keep the lamps. Please keep the peace.
May this road stay open, and kind.
priest.talk: Namaste, {name}. The shrine is quiet if you wish to rest.
priest.rumour: Do not linger near the forge gate after dark. Danger gathers there.

barks: A tale! Of smiths and roads and dawn!
Hush! The hero of this tale is a hammer.
I tell it plain. The listeners make it grand.
Sit, {name}. The best tale is a short one.
A story keeps the forge road company.
Once there was a gate that never shut...
storyteller.talk: A tale, {name}? Of smiths, roads, or the dawn bell?
storyteller.rumour: In my tale the gate holds till the dawn bell. I hope it is true.

barks: Move along. The road belongs to all.
Raiders about. Stay near the crowd.
Keep to the lit lane, {name}.
No fights at the forge, please.
Watch is tight tonight. Help if you can.
Honest folk have nothing to fear.
town_guard.talk: Evening, {name}. The road watch is on duty.
town_guard.rumour: Raiders gather near the forge gate. If you can, help hold it.
